brand: Seek: horizontal strip where a monospace badge (short product code, contained in a thin-bordered capsule) is set inline beside a heavier display-weight wordmark — the mark and the name use different font families with different size and weight by structural jurisdiction, not decoration

Look for: sub-label (version, category, or descriptor) in a third family (small-caps or spaced mono) at a much smaller size, aligned to center or baseline of the strip — functioning as a semantic tier, not an afterthought
Pattern to find: the whole lockup reads as instrument-panel nameplate, not a logo — it is part of the chrome, subordinate to the app, never centered or hero-sized
REJECT if: the brand is isolated, oversized, animated, uses a custom logomark glyph, or fills more than ~30% of the header strip width
step-heads: Seek: large tabular numerals in a monospace or condensed face, amber or accent-tinted, sitting to the left of a two-tier text block (title line + descriptor line) — the number is typographic, NOT enclosed in a bubble, circle, or pill
Pattern: number and title share a BASELINE alignment (not center or top), so the number reads as a column marker in a tight prose grid rather than a milestone badge

Look for: the descriptor line constrained to ~60–70ch, rendered in a secondary weight/color, clearly subordinate — the step-head has three distinct optical weights in three lines: accent numeral → display uppercase title → body-weight description
REJECT if: the number sits inside a circle/badge, if connector lines link the steps (stepper/wizard pattern), or if all three tiers are the same color/weight
terminal-preview: Seek: a framed terminal or code window that is EMBEDDED inside a larger application layout — the frame is part of the configurator UI, not a hero illustration or standalone mockup

The titlebar chrome must be minimal and functional: a left-anchored dot group (3 circles, simple, non-skeuomorphic), a centered title in spaced mono uppercase, and a RIGHT-SIDE interactive control (slider, column picker, or similar) — all three zones present in a single compact bar
Look for: the preview content area rendered DARKER than its frame (ground darker than panel), creating a recessed-instrument reading: the frame housing is warmer/lighter, the output well is deeper
The frame border should be a hairline (1px) — the window reads as an incision in the layout, not a card floating above it — 2px radius or less

REJECT if: the frame is a realistic macOS/Windows chrome illustration, if it uses drop-shadow or glow to lift it, if the dots use actual traffic-light red/yellow/green fills, or if the terminal is used as a decorative hero element

acceptNuance: Single-accent discipline: accept reference UIs where the accent color is NOT amber but is used with the same semantic restraint — one warm-tone accent (ochre, brass, gold, burnt orange) applied only to active state, CTA, and sequence markers, never as background fill or decoration

Grid substrate signal: accept references that show a very faint engineering grid or micro-texture as a page background even if barely visible — this substrate is a load-bearing impeccable cue indicating instrument-grade intent, not minimalism

Three-family typographic jurisdiction: prioritize references that visibly commit three font families to three distinct roles (display for headlines, humanist sans for body, mono for code/labels/status) with NO overlap — the family is the role

Hairline-only separation: accept references that divide sections exclusively with 1px rules and opacity shifts — no filled dividers, no section backgrounds, no shadow-based z-separation; the layout is flat and the rules do the work

Near-zero radius: treat 2px radius as the aesthetic ceiling — any reference using pill-shaped components, large rounded cards (>8px), or capsule-heavy layouts should be REJECTED even if the palette is otherwise correct
